name: Mabe Fratti
label: Unheard of Hope
lede: A cellist raised in a Guatemalan church orchestra went to Mexico City for three months, stayed, and ended up at No. 20 on Pitchfork's 2024 list.

eras.title: Saxophone denied, cello assigned
eras.text: A kid in a neo-pentecostal Guatemalan household gets classical lessons, church-orchestra duty and a Ligeti CD her father brought home. The secular world arrives by file-sharing and Soundcloud.

years.src: Loud and Quiet · Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Mabe Fratti is born in Guatemala
years.p: She starts on the saxophone, loses it to breathing trouble, and lands on the cello at eight in the children's orchestra attached to the national Sinfónica.
years.xp:
Loud and Quiet reports she switched to cello because respiratory problems kept her off saxophone, and that she played in Guatemala's children's orchestra tied to the Sinfónica. Sounds and Colours says she began cello at age eight with an evangelical Christian teacher who played nothing written after 1900.

Wikipedia gives her birth date as February 13, 1992. Her current cello, it adds, was a gift from her school.

years.src: Loud and Quiet · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: A Ligeti CD her father brought home rewires her
years.p: Her dad's stack of discs ran from Christian music and Disney to wolf-howl new age records, and one of them was György Ligeti.
years.xp: Fratti told Loud and Quiet her father's CD piles included animal-sounds new age albums and a Ligeti disc that hit her hard at ten. Wikipedia adds that she later found a Jacqueline du Pré DVD on her own and began composing as a teenager.

q: I guess there was no demon inside me. I was exorcised.
years.src: Loud and Quiet · Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Church orchestra by Sunday, LimeWire by night
years.p: She grows up in a neo-pentecostal church and evangelical school, where, she says, Yu-Gi-Oh was considered satanic, and quietly finds reggae, blues and funk online.
years.xp:
Loud and Quiet reports the community disapproved of secular interests and that church members believed she was possessed. Fratti tells it with a shrug. Wikipedia says she discovered broader music through LimeWire and eventually left the church.

She told Sounds and Colours she began playing in bands in her late teens, and that her parents remain very conservative.

eras.title: Three months that became a city
eras.text: A Goethe-Institut residency drops her in Mexico City, where the experimental venues and DIY scene change what a cellist is allowed to do. A first record follows.

years.big: Three months became six years, and counting.
years.src: Loud and Quiet · Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: A Goethe-Institut residency brings her to Mexico
years.p: A Goethe-Institut rep found her Soundcloud recordings and offered a paid residency in Malinalco; she moved on to Mexico City.
years.xp:
Loud and Quiet reports the Goethe-Institut found her on Soundcloud. She credits Mexico City venues such as Jazzorca and Terraza Monstruo, and the DIY scene around them, with her awakening. Wikipedia says she soon worked with Libertad Figueroa, Gudrun Gut and Julián Bonequi, and met Héctor Tosta and the future members of [[Amor Muere|92d31114-8a7a-4950-a855-985068f9df1c]].

Sounds and Colours quotes her on the move as a whole.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti · Loud and Quiet
years.h: Pies Sobre La Tierra is her first album
years.p: Wikipedia says it takes inspiration from W. G. Sebald's The Rings of Saturn; Loud and Quiet says her first record came out on Hole Records, Tajak's label.
years.xp: She describes her recordings as journal entries documenting moments in her life, per Loud and Quiet.

eras.title: Tin Angel, dryer and dryer
eras.text: Lockdown writing turns into a run of records with guests from Berlin to Milwaukee, then a live breakthrough in Europe. She starts recording with fewer overdubs and less reverb.

years.src: Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.h: Será Que Ahora Podremos Entendernos, written in lockdown
years.p: Claire Rousay is a guest on "Hacia El Vacío" and Tajak appears on the record, according to Wikipedia.
years.xp: Sounds and Colours notes the album was written during lockdown. BBC 6 Music's Mary-Anne Hobbs has said she plays cello like a wild angel.

years.src: Sounds and Colours · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
years.p: Sounds and Colours dates the release to late November 2021 on SA Recordings; Wikipedia lists it as 2022.

q: I wanted it to sound dryer and dryer.
years.src: The Quietus · Levi Dayan · Wikipedia: Mabe Fratti
yt: KEXP session: No Se Ve Desde Acá
years.h: Se Ve Desde Aquí goes dry, on purpose
years.p: She skipped vocal and cello overdubs and spent about $2,000 on microphones; Oneohtrix Point Never called it mind blowing, per Wikipedia.
years.xp:
The Quietus reports the record came out on Tin Angel Records, with Héctor Tosta, drummer Gibrán Andrade, saxophonist Jarrett Gilgore and violinist Alina Maldonado among the players, and Exploded View's Hugo Quezada producing. Fratti mixed her own records and told the magazine the sound kept getting drier.

Levi Dayan's interview adds that the album leaned on long improvisations and hard editing, with wind arrangements by Tosta.

eras.title: Two bands, one partner, No. 20
eras.text: Héctor Tosta, the guitarist and producer who records as I. la Católica, becomes her co-writer in Titanic and the producer of her fourth solo album. Pitchfork puts it on its year-end list.

years.p: A Time to Love, a Time to Die comes from a four-member collective, with Concepción Huerta, Gibrana Cervantes and Camille Mandoki.

years.src: Tin Angel Records: Titanic's Vidrio · BOMB Magazine
years.p: Eight songs of chamber pop and jazz on Tin Angel Records, credited to Titanic, I. la Católica and Mabe Fratti.
years.xp:
The Guardian placed it somewhere between jazz and chamber pop, per Tin Angel's release post. BOMB Magazine later described the duo's work as effortlessly poised and endlessly ambitious.

Tosta handles multi-instrumental work; Fratti writes string arrangements and sings lead.

years.cap: Album art, Sentir Que No Sabes
years.src: Wikipedia: Sentir Que No Sabes · Exclaim! · Treble · The Line of Best Fit
years.h: Sentir Que No Sabes arrives on Unheard of Hope
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4 and ranked it No. 20 of 2024; the Guardian made it album of the week.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists I. La Católica as producer and arranger, with Jacob Wick on trumpet, Gibrán Andrade on drums and Estrella del Sol on whistle. It has a Metacritic score of 86 from ten critics.

Exclaim! hears opener "Kravitz" as a groovy distorted cello stomp; Treble hears horn stabs over an upright bass groove. The Line of Best Fit gave the album 7/10 and found it darker and more industrial than her earlier work.

years.src: Album of the Year · Pitchfork's 50 Best Albums of 2024
years.h: Year-end lists: Loud and Quiet No. 3, Guardian No. 12
years.p: Resident Advisor put it at No. 10, Paste at 17, Beats Per Minute at 20 and Pitchfork at 20, per Album of the Year.

eras.title: Hagen, and back on the road
eras.text: Titanic follow up with a second album and a long European run, including dates supporting Black Country, New Road.

years.src: Stereogum · BOMB Magazine · Tin Angel Records: Titanic announce HAGEN
yt: Mabe Fratti: Desde El Cielo, Live on KEXP
years.p: Daniel Lopatin and Nate Salon play synths on "Pájaro de fuego"; drummer Eli Keszler improvises on "Gotera".
years.xp: Stereogum says the album came out on Unheard of Hope, with "Gotera" as lead single; the song began during a Gaudeamus residency in the Netherlands. BOMB praised Fratti's vocal on "La dueña" as career-best.

years.src: Tin Angel Records: Titanic announce HAGEN
years.h: Titanic hit End of the Road, then the UK and Europe
years.p: The fall tour runs through October 31, with select dates supporting [[Black Country, New Road|e9403d9c-329b-4108-a26f-564159d441d9]].
